detailed_summary:
## OP Intent
- To share a first-time heroin experience, challenge drug misconceptions, and invite questions (AMA). The OP also intends to try cocaine next for comparison, viewing it as an 'experiment and an adventure in life'.

## Reply Clusters
- Warnings and Dangers of Heroin Addiction: Numerous commenters, many with personal experience as former addicts, highlight the extreme addictiveness of heroin, the severity of withdrawal, and how quickly it can ruin lives, often despite initial feelings of control. They caution against further use, emphasizing the deceptive nature of addiction.
- Validation of Heroin's Intense Pleasure and Challenging Addiction Stereotypes: Some users corroborate the OP's description of heroin's profound pleasure, sometimes from personal experience. They also push back against the idea that a single use automatically leads to immediate, irreversible addiction, suggesting that responsible or infrequent use might be possible for some individuals.
- Questions, Advice, and Alternative Drug Suggestions: Commenters seek more details about the OP's experience, offer practical safety advice (e.g., not using alone, researching risks), or suggest other substances like LSD or DMT, often contrasting them with heroin's addictive potential.

### Warnings and Dangers of Heroin Addiction
- Yes, opioid molecules are the best on earth. It really is the greatest feeling life has to offer. Unfortunately once I got a taste for that feeling it was all over. Opioids are the most addictive drugs on the planet. Once your body gets addicted the withdrawl is pure hell.
- Don't do it again. EVER. There is nothing so terrible in this world as heroin withdrawals. It takes doing heroin every day or every other day for about 2-3 months to get your first habit, but that time goes by real fast when you are high. Just leave it alone. Seriously.
- Just wanted to let you know you sound exactly like I did when I first did dope. Same optimistic and sense of self control that us thrill seekers have. Smart enough to rationalize and study exactly what was going on. That was over $500,000 ago. I was a CIO and built a very successful company while hiding track marks. Eventually it all fell apart.
- I'm seeing red flags all over your post, like this: >I have the urge to do it again but I will resist and not do it, **at least not for a long time.**. The problem with opiate addiction is that it creeps up on you in such a subtle way that you won't notice until you're already in deep.
- Whether you know it or not, whether you become addictted or not, you will be chasing that proverbial dragon for the rest of your life. I've seen it happen to so many kids i grew up with, who keep chasing that feeling or whatever it is happened to them when they did heroin or OCs.
- STOP! IMMEDIATELY!! I have done many many drugs, i've dealt drugs when I was younger, but I have never seen something ruin so many friends lives like herion. if you get hooked on herion, you get hooked and if you step up to injecting it is VERY hard to stop. Herion is no joke, it is not a casual drug.
- Fuck heroin. It's awesome. Too awesome. The only reason I stopped is because I lost two good friends to it. One died after an OD. The other is still alive, but he's all but a vegetable.

### Validation of Heroin's Intense Pleasure and Challenging Addiction Stereotypes
- Yes, opioid molecules are the best on earth. It really is the greatest feeling life has to offer.
- Thanks for doing your best to combat the myth that you'll be ZOMG ADDICTED HOMELESS JUNKIE after one hit; it doesn't work that way. I've never done street heroin but I've experimented with plenty of similar drugs (particularly Oramorph, which is seriously good shit if you can get hold of it) to know what it'd be like.
- I chased the dragon in amsterdam in 1987. after the hurling was over, the "i couldn't possibly care about anything" feeling kicked in, and i'll never forget it. but i don't regret it one bit, just like you.
- I have to agree with you, OP, the feeling of heroin is second to none.
- I totally relate to your experience. In the heat of the moment, I did heroin. It was great. I would use all the words you used to describe it, including all the 'red flags' and what not. It can almost seem insulting to ones level of control, if they truly do have that discipline.
- I just had my wisdom teeth out and got 10mg oxycodone pills, which is basically synthetic heroin. I took them for funzies a few times after my mouth healed. It was great, I felt on top of the world, outgoing, full of happiness and good will! That being said, and despite the fact I'd love to feel that way again, I have no intentions of ever searching for any, and if the opportunity came up I probably wouldn't even buy any. I completely understand the OP and can relate. Maybe we're just blessed with nonaddictive personalities.

### Questions, Advice, and Alternative Drug Suggestions
- Can you please describe the sensation with more detail? What kind of pleasure did you feel? How did it affect your state of mind and train of thought? Can you compare it to any familiar sensations (in quality, not intensity)?
- hypothetically, if you were to become addicted, what would be the first thing you'd pawn off for money?
- Was there a bad hangover?
- It's really stupid to do heroin alone, especially the first time. Don't do that again! People die! Trust me, I know.
- Try LSD. mind expanding, zero addiction, life changing. Pierce the illusion.
- If you use a needle it is even BETTER. Using heroin as a recreational drug is just such a great idea.
- Try some DMT

## Counterarguments
- Multiple former addicts directly counter the OP's perceived self-control and optimism, stating that they had similar mindsets before addiction took hold, and that the drug's addictive nature creeps up subtly.
- The OP's assertion that they will resist further use is questioned, with commenters pointing out the 'red flags' in their language (e.g., 'at least not for a long time') and asking if they could truly refuse if offered again.
- The OP's view that heroin is not the 'most addictive drug' is contradicted by some who call opioids the 'most addictive drugs on the planet' and emphasize heroin's unique physical addiction.
- The OP's idea of heroin as a 'valuable life experience' is implicitly countered by those who express deep regret for their past drug use and the destruction it caused.
- The OP's comparison of cocaine to heroin and intent to try coke is met with warnings about cocaine's own addictive potential and dangers, despite its 'socially acceptable' image in some circles.

## Unresolved Questions
- Did you eat the fucking fries or what?
- Was there a bad hangover?
- How often do you find yourself thinking about your experience since your use?
- Did you feel any negative effects stemming from your use? Physically/mentally?
- Why would you consider doing it again?
- Did you remember the whole experience, or do you feel like you were unaware during most of it?
- Do you feel like you could have done anything besides sitting on the couch while doing it (reading, writing, solving the world's problems etc)?
- So which is worse - heroin or Reddit?
- Compare and contrast with pot? Feelings, mental state, after effects, price?
- Have you already been walking by the park again after your experience and, if yes, how you felt about it?
- Did you get nauseous at all?
- Are you normally a high risk taker or is this a phase?
- Looking back at it, do you find heroin 'boring'?
